commit.message:
security: extend CWE-73 fix to main MCP saveVectorToFile/loadVectorFromFile

While auditing the path-traversal bug from issue #19, found the exact
same sink class in `src/mcp/server.ts`:

  - `saveVectorToFile` accepts an MCP-callable `file_path`, runs
    `path.resolve(filePath)` (which silently resolves absolute paths,
    `../` segments, and traversal payloads), `mkdirSync(recursive: true)`
    the parent, and writes via `fs.writeFileSync`. An attacker could
    overwrite any file the MCP process could touch.

  - `loadVectorFromFile` is the symmetric read sink — caller-controlled
    `file_path` reads via `fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(filePath))`,
    letting an attacker exfiltrate any file the MCP process could read.

Fix: new `src/mcp/safe-path.ts` enforces the same basename-only contract
as the consciousness-explorer fix, with a separate vector directory
($SUBLINEAR_SOLVER_VECTOR_DIR or ~/.sublinear-time-solver/vectors) so
test vectors and consciousness snapshots don't share a namespace.

Both `saveVectorToFile` and `loadVectorFromFile` now route through
safeWriteVector / safeReadVector, which:
  * reject path separators, "..", leading ".", control chars, NUL,
    Windows-reserved device names, oversize basenames;
  * recompute the realpath and refuse anything that escapes the vector
    dir even after path normalisation;
  * open with O_NOFOLLOW + O_CLOEXEC + 0o600 mode so a symlink at the
    final component can't redirect the I/O.

The MCP tool schema for `saveVectorToFile` advertises the new contract
via JSON Schema `pattern`, `minLength`, `maxLength` so MCP clients see
the constraint at tool-list time.

Defence in depth — extends issue #19. No new public CVE yet because the
upstream report covered consciousness-explorer; this is the maintainer
closing the rest of the sink class.
